key_insight: AI in medical imaging grew rapidly from 2017–2025, and UK research showed strong citation efficiency and increasing influence, especially around generative and foundation-based methods.
clinical_relevance: This is a bibliometric study, so it informs how imaging AI research is evolving rather than providing direct patient-care guidance.
method: Scopus-indexed publications from 2017–2025 were searched for AI and medical imaging terms, including generative and foundation-based keywords.
Global output was compared with UK-affiliated publications using publication counts, citations, citations per paper, and yearly growth.
Co-authorship and keyword networks were mapped with VOSviewer to identify collaboration patterns and research themes.
evidence_signal: The analysis identified 13,452 global papers with 194,650 citations, including 889 UK-affiliated papers, and found UK citations per paper were higher than many higher-volume countries.
watch_item: Recent citation growth may be underestimated because newer papers have not had time to accumulate citations, so impact should be interpreted with a citation-lag in mind.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging With Emphasis on Generative and Foundation-Based Methods: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global and United Kingdom Research, 2017-2025
